question: What is a primary requirement before initiating any diagnostic reproductive procedure?
explanation: Valid informed consent ensures the patient understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives before any procedure takes place. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is psychological support particularly vital during reproductive diagnostic evaluations?

options.A: Anxiety physically blocks the absorption of contrast dyes
options.B: Patients are legally mandated to receive counseling first
options.C: Hormonal assays cannot be processed if the patient is stressed
options.D: Reproductive organs carry high cultural and emotional significance

explanation: Issues surrounding fertility, sexuality, and reproductive health frequently trigger deep emotional distress and anxiety, requiring empathetic nursing care. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h1)

question: On which day of the menstrual cycle is serum Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) traditionally measured to assess ovarian reserve?
explanation: Day three FSH levels give an accurate baseline reading of ovarian function and reserve. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h2)

question: What does a mid-luteal serum progesterone test primarily confirm?
explanation: Progesterone rises significantly after ovulation, making its mid-luteal measurement a reliable marker that ovulation took place. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary diagnostic purpose of a Hysterosalpingography (HSG)?

options.B: Evaluating uterine cavity shape and Fallopian tube patency
options.C: Screening for cervical dysplasia and human papillomavirus

explanation: HSG uses contrast dye and X-rays to outline the inside of the uterus and determine if the fallopian tubes are open. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for a Hysterosalpingography expresses fear of sharp cramping pain during the dye injection. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Inform her that cramping only happens if a tube is permanently blocked
options.B: Cancel the procedure immediately and request an MRI instead
options.C: Reassure her that the procedure is completely painless because anesthesia is used
options.D: Advise the patient that mild analgesics are often prescribed beforehand to manage cramping

explanation: Contrast injection triggers uterine contractions resembling strong menstrual cramps, which can be mitigated with preemptive analgesics. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which diagnostic instrument is inserted through the cervical os to directly inspect the interior of the uterus?
explanation: A hysteroscope is specifically designed to pass through the cervix and visualize the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the underlying cause of shoulder-tip pain following a diagnostic laparoscopy?

options.A: Muscle strain from lying flat on the operating table for too long
options.B: Referred cardiac pain caused by intravenous line placement
options.C: Irritation of the diaphragm by residual insufflated carbon dioxide gas
options.D: Internal bruising of the uterine ligaments during manipulation

explanation: Trapped carbon dioxide gas presses against the diaphragm, causing referred pain that travels up to the shoulder. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical objective of a Pap smear?

options.B: Confirming the presence of tubal occlusion
options.D: Detecting pre-cancerous cellular changes in the cervix

explanation: Cytological examination of cervical cells identifies dysplasia before it develops into invasive cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is acetic acid applied to the cervix during a colposcopy examination?

options.A: It dissolves thick mucus plugs blocking the view of the transformation zone
options.B: It causes abnormal or dysplastic cellular areas to turn white for targeted biopsy
options.C: It sterilizes the vaginal vault to prevent post-procedure infection
options.D: It completely numbs the cervical tissue to eliminate biopsy pain

explanation: Acetic acid temporarily coagulates cellular proteins in abnormal tissue, causing them to appear white (acetowhite) so the clinician can target the biopsy accurately. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence prior to providing a semen sample for analysis?
explanation: A 2 to 5 day window ensures an accurate assessment of sperm count, motility, and morphology without compromising quality. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a major advantage of measuring Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) over Day 3 FSH when evaluating ovarian reserve?

options.A: AMH definitively confirms the exact date of menopause
options.B: AMH can only be measured using urine samples
options.C: AMH levels remain relatively stable throughout the menstrual cycle
options.D: AMH testing requires no laboratory processing

explanation: Unlike cycle-dependent hormones like FSH, AMH can be drawn on any day of the cycle, offering a consistent marker of ovarian reserve. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h6)

question: A patient who underwent a diagnostic hysteroscopy two days ago calls the clinic reporting a foul-smelling vaginal discharge and low-grade fever. What is the most appropriate nursing interpretation?

options.A: This is a normal healing response following cervical manipulation
options.B: This indicates the body is successfully eliminating residual contrast dye
options.C: The patient should be advised to insert antiseptic vaginal suppositories
options.D: These signs suggest an ascending pelvic infection requiring medical evaluation

explanation: Fever and foul-smelling discharge are classic indicators of infection following instrumentation of the reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which instruction is most critical for a nurse to include in the discharge education for a patient who just had an endometrial biopsy?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake for forty-eight hours to reduce uterine cramping
options.B: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampon use until the cervix is fully healed
options.C: Perform daily vaginal douches with warm saline solution
options.D: Expect heavy bleeding that requires changing pads every thirty minutes

explanation: Pelvic rest prevents bacteria from entering the open cervical os and causing endometritis or pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h7)
